nodes.label: Basic Bot Filtering (FR-011)
nodes.rationale: Perfect bot detection is not required; bot interactions just must not appear in default merchant analytics.

nodes.label: Business (FR-004)
nodes.rationale: Deletion is soft deletion via archived_at.

nodes.label: Card (FR-007)
nodes.rationale: Must not expose sequential database IDs; use random secure IDs (NanoID or UUID-derived slug), 6-10 characters.

nodes.label: Card Inventory Code (FR-021, RT-XXXXXX)
nodes.rationale: Separate from customer-facing branding; used to identify cards during support, track inventory, replace damaged cards, and reassign cards.

nodes.label: Google Reviews (Destination)
nodes.rationale: Google Reviews is the initial wedge; future destinations (Instagram, WhatsApp, menus, loyalty, CRM) are explicitly deferred out of V1.

nodes.label: Interaction Tracking (FR-010)
nodes.rationale: Store only card_id, source, timestamp minimum; do not store unnecessary personally identifying data (privacy by minimization).

nodes.label: Manual Card Assignment (FR-020)
nodes.rationale: Particularly important during pilots: admin pre-creates physical card inventory and assigns to business/location/placement, which dramatically simplifies deployment.

nodes.label: Merchant Funnel (Product Analytics, Section 29)
nodes.rationale: Critical activation event is the first real card interaction.

nodes.label: North Star Metric: Monthly Review Page Visits
nodes.rationale: Measures whether the product is actually being used in the physical world.
nodes.norm_label: north star metric: monthly review page visits

nodes.label: NTAG213 NFC Chip
nodes.rationale: Chosen because it is inexpensive, broadly compatible, has sufficient memory, and is suitable for URL storage.

nodes.label: Onboarding Wizard (FR-017)
nodes.rationale: Target: new merchant configures first digital card in under 3 minutes; business owners frequently operate from phones so UI must be mobile-first.

nodes.label: Organization (FR-003)
nodes.rationale: Organization layer introduced above Business even though V1 users typically own a single business, to prevent future data restructuring.

nodes.label: QR Generator (FR-015)
nodes.rationale: QR generation must not rely on an external third-party service; must support SVG and PNG with sufficient error correction to remain scannable when printed.

nodes.label: Redirect Endpoint (FR-009: GET /q/:publicId, GET /n/:publicId)
nodes.rationale: Redirect customer takes priority over recording analytics; logging failure should never prevent the customer reaching Google. Log asynchronously / fire-and-forget, then 302 redirect.

nodes.label: Review Page Visits (FR-013 Primary Metric)
nodes.rationale: Never label interactions as 'Reviews generated' unless ReviewTap can prove a review was submitted; use Review Page Visits / Card Interactions / QR Scans / NFC Taps instead.

nodes.label: ReviewTap (Product)
nodes.rationale: V1 goal is not a complete reputation-management platform; it validates that businesses use the product, keep cards deployed, care about analytics, and eventually pay.

nodes.label: SVG/PNG QR Generator + Print Card Generator
nodes.norm_label: svg/png qr generator + print card generator

nodes.label: getCards({ orgId }) Post-Join JS Filtering
nodes.rationale: Correct but unbounded at scale; revisit when card count makes dashboard latency noticeable.

nodes.label: Service-Role Client for All App Queries (dbRepo getAdminClient)
nodes.rationale: Deliberate known limitation: service role bypasses RLS so tenant isolation rests entirely on app-level checks; revisit when onboarding non-pilot customers — fix is a user-scoped Supabase client for merchant routes while keeping service role for /q, /n, platform admin, and system tasks.
nodes.norm_label: service-role client for all app queries (dbrepo getadminclient)

nodes.label: Tenant Isolation in App Code (Route-Level Ownership Pre-Checks)
nodes.norm_label: tenant isolation in app code (route-level ownership pre-checks)

nodes.label: PRD — Smart Review Card Platform V1
nodes.norm_label: prd — smart review card platform v1

nodes.label: README — ReviewTap Smart NFC & QR Review Infrastructure
nodes.norm_label: readme — reviewtap smart nfc & qr review infrastructure

nodes.label: Destination Validation (SR-004)
nodes.rationale: Only https:// scheme approved; javascript:, file:, data: schemes must be blocked.

nodes.label: Object Authorization (SR-002)
nodes.rationale: Every request for business, location, card, or analytics must validate organization membership; never trust frontend identifiers.

nodes.label: Open Redirect Protection (SR-005)
nodes.rationale: Redirect URL must never come from query parameters; destination must always come from server-side database configuration to prevent open-redirect abuse.

nodes.label: Redirect Architecture (Core Product Principle)
nodes.rationale: QR code and NFC tag must never directly encode the Google Review URL — both encode a ReviewTap-owned redirect URL so the destination can be changed remotely, cards never need reprinting or reprogramming, interactions are measurable, cards can be disabled/tracked/reassigned, and businesses depend on the software rather than the NFC hardware.

nodes.label: V1 Non-Goals (Section 33)
nodes.rationale: AI review generation/replies, sentiment analysis, WhatsApp automation, CRM, loyalty, custom landing pages, POS integration, review scraping, Stripe automation, mobile app, white-label, third-party API are all excluded because each creates scope creep before product-market validation.

nodes.label: Rate Limiting (SR-006)
nodes.rationale: Basic limits on login, signup, card creation, and redirect endpoints if abuse occurs; redirect rate limiting must not affect legitimate high-volume business usage.

nodes.label: Per-Instance Rate Limiter (src/lib/rate-limiter.ts)
nodes.rationale: Best-effort abuse friction only; replace with Upstash Redis (@upstash/ratelimit) when anything billable or security-relevant depends on it.

nodes.label: Threat Model (V1 Pilot)
nodes.rationale: Merants and anonymous visitors hold the public anon key and can hit Supabase REST directly, not just through the app UI; the service-role key must never leave the server.
